page: Microsoft Azure D32as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 32 vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz, backed by dedicated CPU allocation. It is equipped with 128 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4 GB per vCPU. Cache hierarchy consists of 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2, though AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, requiring external Premium Storage attachments, and no dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core processing ranking in the top tier, supported by strong PassMark memory marks and high Geekbench image processing throughput. Small-model LLM generation also demonstrates strong execution rates. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks—such as Geekbench multi-core, passmark CPU evaluations, and stress-ng multi-core testing—remain in the middle tier. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 74.32 GB/s for reads and 44.85 GB/s for writes. The absence of AVX-512 extensions and dedicated GPU acceleration severely limits performance on heavy tensor operations, as shown by weak inference processing on large 70B parameter models.

In terms of resource efficiency, the D32as_v5 offers balanced CPU and memory density suitable for multi-threaded workloads that do not require specialized accelerator hardware. Because it lacks onboard ephemeral storage, the platform avoids bundled disk overhead while directing storage-dependent operations to network-attached drives. This configuration is appropriate for distributed web services, software compilation with Clang, containerized microservices, Redis caching layers, and general enterprise backend processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D32as_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 3.525 GHz AMD EPYC 7763 processor with dedicated allocation under Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 32 MB of L3 cache, and 128 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The architecture supports AVX and hardware-accelerated cryptography, but excludes AVX-512, AMX, and GPUs. No local storage is bundled, necessitating external network volumes. Benchmark metrics indicate strong single-core stress-ng throughput and PassMark memory performance, while multi-core execution, Redis throughput, and web serving benchmarks sit within standard median ranges. Due to the lack of specialized hardware accelerators, heavy matrix computations and 70B LLM tasks yield weak results. Delivering solid resource balance, the D32as_v5 is suitable for software compilation pipelines, enterprise web backends, caching services, and microservices workloads.
